question: Is 1024-entry oldest-entry eviction acceptable for Google Chat approval-card bindings and manual follow-up suppressions?
rationale: Automation can review the code shape, but it cannot choose the product threshold or approve making very old pending approval state unresolvable before expiry under extreme concurrent Google Chat approval load.

options.title: Accept 1024 after proof
options.body: Keep this implementation if the contributor posts redacted real behavior proof and maintainers accept early eviction beyond 1024 registry entries.

options.title: Tune the eviction policy
options.body: Ask for a higher threshold, different eviction rule, or follow-up instrumentation if pending approval lifetime should be protected more strongly under bursty workloads.

options.title: Defer the cap
options.body: Leave the PR open or close it if bounded memory is not worth changing high-cardinality approval-card lifetime semantics now.

recommendation.title: Accept 1024 after proof
recommendation.body: Keep this implementation if the contributor posts redacted real behavior proof and maintainers accept early eviction beyond 1024 registry entries.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored and merged the native Google Chat approval-card feature whose registry lifetime behavior is being changed.
